title: Elector-based capacity routing with grace windows and eviction budgets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a low-latency decision layer that chooses between tenant-dedicated capacity and hosted spillover without causing capacity thrash, availability regressions, or large customer bill surprises. Current heuristics (simple reserved-first then fallback) lead to oscillations during short spikes and poor tail latency when eviction is aggressive.

Proposal: Implement an "elector" decision function that combines (1) capacity score (available slots, recent load), (2) tenant SLA priority, (3) model-variant compatibility, and (4) eviction budget to decide routing. Add a configurable grace window and eviction budget per-tenant that prevents immediate eviction of recent reservations for short bursts. Integrate a circuit-breaker hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping between dedicated and hosted.

Key behaviors to implement: 1) Elector picks dedicated when capacity_score >= dedicated_threshold OR when tenant has soft-reserve credits; 2) Probabilistic spillover path when capacity_score in a defined buffer range to gently shed load to hosted without bulk migration; 3) Eviction budget that charges an "eviction burn" counter and disallows further evictions until budget replenishes; 4) Grace window (default 15s) that pins active slots for in-flight sessions to avoid tail-latency regressions; 5) Variant compatibility check to only route to hosted when model variant fallbacks are validated for prompt-length and KV-cache semantics.

Operational signals and telemetry: expose elector_decision_reason, capacity_score, eviction_burn_level, grace_window_active, and variant_compat_score. Add dashboards and alerts for increased probabilistic_spill_rate, sustained eviction_burn, and repeated elector flip events.

Why this is different: The elector is a single, auditable decision function (not a set of hard-coded guards) and supports tunable smoothing primitives (grace windows, budgets, probabilistic routing) to trade cost vs SLOs in a controlled way.
acceptance_criteria: Elector decision API implemented and callable by routing plane (feature-flagged)
Grace window and eviction budget honoured end-to-end (unit + e2e tests)
Probabilistic spillover path can be tuned per-tenant and has rollout knobs
Variant compatibility matrix prevents routing to hosted for incompatible KV-cache/model combos
Telemetry keys present in Console: elector_decision_reason, capacity_score, eviction_burn_level, grace_window_active
Canary rollout completed against 5 pilot tenants with no SLO regressions for 72h
